title: H 3418 (118th General Assembly): A Bill Relating To Reform Of The South Carolina Election Laws By Enacting The "south Carolina Election Reform Act"; To Amend Section 7-13-710 Of The 1976 Code To Require Photograph Identification To Vote, Permitting For Provisional Ballots If The Identification Cannot Be Produced And Provide An Exception For A Religious Objection To Being Photographed; To Amend Section 56-1-3350 To Require The Department Of Motor Vehicles To Provide Free Identification Cards Upon Request; To Amend Section 7-13-25 To Provide For An Early Voting Period Beginning Sixteen Days Before A Statewide Primary Or General Election And To Provide For The Hours And Early Voting Location; To Amend Section 7-3-20(c) To Require The Executive Director Of The State Elections Commission To Maintain In The Master File A Separate Designation For Absentee And Early Voters In A General Election; To Amend Section 7-15-30 To Add Statutory Cites Regarding The Request Of An Absentee Ballot; To Amend Section 7-15-470 To Provide For Early Voting On Machines During The Early Voting Period Only And Delete The Reference To Absentee Voting; To Amend Section 7-1-25 To List Factors To Consider For Domicile; And To Amend Section 7-5-230 To Reference Revisions To Section 7-1-25.
operative_text:
(a_in_person_id)
(section) SECTION 1, amending S.C. Code 7-13-710(A)
(quote) When a person presents himself to vote, he shall produce a valid and current: (1) South Carolina driver's license; (2) other form of identification containing a photograph issued by the Department of Motor Vehicles; (3) passport; (4) military identification containing a photograph issued by the federal government; or (5) South Carolina voter registration card containing a photograph of the voter pursuant to Section 7-5-675.
(section) SECTION 1, 7-13-710(B)
(quote) One of the managers also shall compare the photograph contained on the required identification with the person presenting himself to vote. The manager shall verify that the photograph is that of the person seeking to vote.
(b_no_id_remedy)
(section) SECTION 1, 7-13-710(C)(1)
(quote) If the elector cannot produce the identification as required in subsection (A), he may cast a provisional ballot that is counted only if the elector brings a valid and current photo identification to the county board of registration and elections before certification of the election by the county board of canvassers.
(section) SECTION 1, 7-13-710(C)(2)
(quote) If the manager disputes that the photograph contained on the required identification is the person presenting himself to vote, the elector may cast a provisional ballot. A determination of that provisional ballot must be made in accordance with Section 7-13-830.
(section) SECTION 1, 7-13-710(D)(1)(a)
(quote) If an elector does not produce a valid and current photograph identification due to a religious objection to being photographed, he may complete an affidavit under penalty of perjury at the polling place and affirm that the elector: (i) is the same individual who personally appeared at the polling place; (ii) cast the provisional ballot on election day; and (iii) has a religious objection to being photographed. Upon completion of the affidavit, the elector may cast a provisional ballot.
(section) SECTION 1, 7-13-710(D)(1)(b)
(quote) If an elector does not produce a valid and current photograph identification because the elector suffers from a reasonable impediment that prevents the elector from obtaining photograph identification, he may complete an affidavit under the penalty of perjury at the polling place and affirm that the elector: (i) is the same individual who personally appeared at the polling place; (ii) cast the provisional ballot on election day; and (iii) the elector suffers from a reasonable impediment that prevents him from obtaining photograph identification.
(section) SECTION 1, 7-13-710(D)(2)
(quote) If the county board of registration and elections determines that the voter was challenged only for the inability to provide proof of identification and the required affidavit is submitted, the county board of registration and elections shall find that the provisional ballot is valid unless the board has grounds to believe the affidavit is false.
(section) SECTION 3, amending 56-1-3350(B)(2)
(quote) An identification card must be free to a person aged seventeen years or older.
(c_mail_ballot_id) not stated.
(d_proof_of_citizenship) not stated.
(e_other_rule)
(section) SECTION 11, new 7-5-675
(quote) The State Elections Commission shall implement a system in order to issue voter registration cards with a photograph of the elector.
(section) SECTION 13
(quote) The State Election Commission is directed to create a list containing all registered voters of South Carolina who are otherwise qualified to vote but do not have a South Carolina driver's license or other form of identification containing a photograph issued by the Department of Motor Vehicles as of January 1, 2012. The list must be made available to a registered voter upon request.
(section) SECTION 12(8)
(quote) Notify each registered elector who does not have a South Carolina issued driver's license or identification card a notice of the provisions of this act by no later than October 15, 2011. This notice must include the requirements to vote absentee, early, or on election day and a description of voting by provisional ballot.
(section) SECTION 18
(quote) Except as otherwise provided in this act, this act takes effect upon approval by the Governor, except that SECTION 1 is effective upon preclearance approval by the United States Department of Justice.
(other) SECTION 1: 7-13-710 photo ID to vote in person, provisional ballot, religious-objection and reasonable-impediment affidavits (slots a, b).
(other) SECTION 2: 7-5-125 written notification of registration; elector who loses it may get a duplicate by request in person, phone or mail.
(other) SECTION 3: 56-1-3350 DMV special ID card: fee five dollars for ages 5-16, free at 17 and older; under-21 cards marked; strikes the old indigent/homeless fee-waiver text and the fee-split table.
(other) SECTION 4: new 7-13-25 early voting at one county early voting center, from the Thursday before a statewide primary or general election to the following Saturday; hours; one ballot only; misdemeanor warning sign.
(other) SECTION 5: 7-3-20(C) State Election Commission executive director enters a separate designation for absentee and early voters in the master file.
(other) SECTION 6: 7-15-320 absentee categories unchanged except adds state election commission staff; adds that a qualified elector may vote during the early voting period.
(other) SECTION 7: 7-15-330 absentee application: request in person or by mail (strikes telephone and strikes the authorized-representative request rules); application deadlines; record book; penalties.
(other) SECTION 8: 7-15-385 return of absentee ballot (authorization to return, no candidate or paid staff as returnee unless family, oath and witness, locked storage).
(other) SECTION 9: 7-1-25 domicile factors list (tax return address, real estate, mailing address, driver's licence address and others).
(other) SECTION 10: 7-5-230 board of registration judges qualifications; written challenges; residence/domicile challenges use the 7-1-25(D) factors.
(other) SECTION 11: new 7-5-675 photo voter registration cards.
(other) SECTION 12: State Election Commission voter-education programme.
(other) SECTION 13: list of registered voters without DMV photo ID.
(other) SECTION 14: single-subject finding. SECTION 15: non-severability clause (whole act falls if any part held invalid).
(other) SECTION 16: repeals 7-15-470 (voting machines for absentee voting).
(other) SECTION 17: SECTION 11 effective July 1, 2011, subject to funding. SECTION 18: act effective on Governor's approval, except SECTION 1 on U.S. Department of Justice preclearance.

Positions are 0-based in the votes array. Two roll calls in the journals are not in the votes list: House second reading 2009-02-26 (Yeas 65, Nays 14, HJ-99) and House adoption of the Conference Report 2010-06-15 (Yeas 69, Nays 47); also no roll call is listed for House 2009 Amendments 8, 9, 10 or 18-23 (not checked whether they were voted by voice), and the Senate second-reading vote 2010-01-28 (36-2) is absent. Journal pages for votes with several similar roll calls were matched by the printed tally.
